parts.text:
11 The diagram shows four forces applied to a circular object.
45 N
30 N
30 N
45 N
Which row describes the resultant force and resultant torque on the object?
resultant force
resultant torque
A
non-zero
non-zero
B
non-zero
zero
C
zero
non-zero
D
zero
zero

hints: Add the vectors separately: compare the $45\text{ N}$ up arrow with the $45\text{ N}$ down arrow, then add the two $30\text{ N}$ arrows to the right.
For torque about the centre, use $torque = F \times$ perpendicular distance and check the turning sense of each tangent force.
Notice the two $30\text{ N}$ forces act at the top and bottom and turn opposite ways, while the two $45\text{ N}$ forces act on opposite sides and turn the same way.
walkthrough: Resolve vertically: $45\text{ N}$ up and $45\text{ N}$ down are equal and opposite, so vertical resultant is $45-45 = 0\text{ N}$.
Resolve horizontally: both $30\text{ N}$ forces act to the right, so horizontal resultant is $30+30 = 60\text{ N}$ to the right.
Hence the vector sum of forces is non-zero at $60\text{ N}$ to the right.
Consider torque about the centre: each force acts tangentially at distance $r$, the radius, so magnitude is $F r$.
The top $30\text{ N}$ and bottom $30\text{ N}$ produce opposite senses and cancel, but the left $45\text{ N}$ up and right $45\text{ N}$ down both produce the same clockwise turning effect.
Total torque is therefore $45r+45r \neq 0$, so resultant torque is non-zero.
Non-zero resultant force with non-zero resultant torque matches the first row. This is option A.

A.explanation: Horizontal $30\text{ N}+30\text{ N}$ gives a non-zero resultant force and the two $45\text{ N}$ forces give a non-zero resultant clockwise torque.

B.explanation: Resultant force is non-zero, but the $45\text{ N}$ up on the left and $45\text{ N}$ down on the right both turn the disc the same way so torque does not cancel to zero.

C.explanation: Vertical forces cancel, but the two $30\text{ N}$ forces to the right add to $60\text{ N}$, so resultant force is not zero.

D.explanation: Neither quantity is zero because horizontal forces add and the $45\text{ N}$ couple adds.
